To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dendritic knobs (dendritic tips) of olfactory sensory neurones (OSNs) expressing the same odorant receptors (ORs) can have different responses to a given odorant, and that these differences are due to different expression of the transduction machinery.

the dendrites of olfactory sensory cells expressing the odorant MOR23 can be patched in a mouse olfactory epithelium, that these cells respond to the odorant lyral, and that there is a wide range of responses to the same odorant among these cells.
the dendrites of olfactory sensory neurones that express the same olfactory receptor have different electrophysiological and pharmacological properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular basis for the sense of smell.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of olfactory signal transduction and the coding of odors in the olfactory system.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the coding of olfactory information in the mammalian brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MOR23 receptor is expressed in a subset of olfactory sensory cells that respond to a variety of odorants with different response kinetics and sensitivities.
the MOR23-expressing OSNs have a very broad dynamic range and that there is a substantial degree of heterogeneity among the OSNs in their response kinetics.
there is a wide range of responses to a given ligand among the neurons that express a given receptor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ORs are not the only determinant of the functional properties of OSNs, but they are the most important determinant.
the OSNs that express OR MOR23 are very sensitive to lyra and have a broad dynamic range.
MOR23 is a high affinity, broad range, and slow receptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a great deal of heterogeneity in the response properties of OSNs expressing the same OR.
OSNs expressing the same OR can have very different odor responses, and this is not simply due to differences in expression level of the receptor.
OSNs expressing the same OR can have very different response properties, which is likely to be an important factor in determining the coding properties of olfactory glomeruli.
